title: 1953 AHSME Problem 31
statement: The rails on a railroad are \(30\) feet long. As the train passes over the point where the rails are joined, there is an audible click. The speed of the train in miles per hour is approximately the number of clicks heard in:

solutions.text:
A speed of \(v\) miles per hour is \(\frac{22v}{15}\) feet per second. Since each click represents \(30\) feet, the click rate is \[ \frac{\frac{22v}{15}}{30}=\frac{11v}{225} \] clicks per second. In \(\frac{225}{11}\approx20.45\) seconds, the number of clicks is \(v.\) The closest listed interval is \(20\) seconds.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Convert one mile per hour to feet per second, then divide by \(30\) feet per click
Find the time interval for which the click count is approximately the numerical speed in miles per hour
